title: Grade 10 Physics National Exam & Practice 2014 (6 Chapters Combined)
description: Comprehensive examination bank combining 6 chapters (100 questions). Official Ethiopian national curriculum.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true about satellite motion?
options: satellite moving closer to the Earth takes longer time to complete one revolution than a satellite farther from the Earth.
For two satellites moving around the Earth at equal orbital radius, a heavier satellite has larger speed than a lighter one.
For equal orbital radius, a satellite moving around the Earth has smaller speed than a satellite moving about Moon.
satellite closer to Earth is faster than a satellite farther from the Earth.
questions.explanation:
According to orbital mechanics, the orbital speed of a satellite is given by:- 

v = √(GM/r), where r is the distance from the center of the Earth.

 Therefore, a satellite closer to Earth (smaller r) moves faster than one farther away.

questions.questionText: A satellite revolves around the Earth in a circular orbit of radius r = 4 * 10¹⁶m. The period of the satellite is ______.
questions.explanation:
The period T of a satellite in a circular orbit is given by:- 

T = 2π√(r³ / GM), 
where G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg² and M = 5.97 × 10²⁴ kg (mass of Earth).

 Substituting r = 4 × 10¹⁶ m gives T ≈ 2.5 × 10¹⁹ s.

questions.questionText: One of the following statements is a correct description of the charging processes?
options: During charging a neutral object by induction using a negatively charged rod, charge flows from the rod to the object.
When a neutral metallic sphere is charged by induction using a negatively charged rod, the sphere acquires a net negative charge.
When a positively charged object is momentarily brought into contact with a neutral metallic sphere, the sphere acquires a net positive charge.
When a plastic rod is rubbed with wool, the two objects acquire a net charge of the same sign.
questions.explanation: Touching a neutral sphere with a positive object removes electrons, so the sphere becomes positive.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is correct about the resistance of a conductor with a circular cross-section?
options: At a given temperature, the resistance of copper and silver wires of the same length and diameter is the same.
The resistance of the conductor increases as its length increases and its diameter decreases.
The resistance of the conductor increases as its length and diameter increases.
The resistance of the conductor decreases as it is heated.
questions.explanation:
The resistance of a conductor is given by R = ρL/A, where ρ is the resistivity, L is the length, and A is the cross-sectional area.

 For a circular cross-section, A ∝ diameter².

 Therefore, resistance increases with length and decreases with diameter.

 Heating generally increases resistance.

questions.questionText: The primary coil of a transformer has 250 turns and its secondary coil consists of 1500 turns. If 220 V is applied to its primary coil, the voltage induced in the secondary coil and the ratio of current in the primary coil to the current in the secondary coil, respectively, are ______.
questions.explanation:
For an ideal transformer, Vₛ / Vₚ = Nₛ / Nₚ and Iₚ / Iₛ = Nₛ / Nₚ.

Here, Nₚ = 250, Nₛ = 1500, Vₚ = 220 V.

Vₛ = (Nₛ / Nₚ) × Vₚ = (1500 / 250) × 220 = 6 × 220 = 1320 V.

The current ratio Iₚ / Iₛ = Nₛ / Nₚ = 1500 / 250 = 6.

questions.questionText: A diode is an electronic component that ______.
options: is useful to convert a DC voltage to AC voltage.
allows electric current to pass through in one direction.
allows the flow of current when its p-type region is connected to the negative terminal of a cell.
allows current to pass through it either from cathode to anode or from anode to cathode.
questions.explanation:
A diode is a semiconductor device that acts as a one-way switch for current.

 It is primarily designed to allow current to flow easily in one direction (forward bias) and to block current flow in the opposite direction (reverse bias). 

This property makes it essential for rectification (converting AC to pulsing DC).

questions.questionText: Suppose a triangular object (O) is placed in front of a plane mirror and its image is formed at position (I). Which one of the following diagrams represents the image (I) formed by the mirror when it is observed from position (X)?
questions.explanation:
A plane mirror forms a virtual image that is the same size as the object, located the same distance behind the mirror, and is laterally inverted (left and right reversed).

 Diagram D correctly shows the image (I) as a lateral reversal of the object (O) at an equal distance from the mirror.

questions.questionText: An object is placed 25.0 cm in front of a concave mirror having focal length of 10.0 cm. The magnification of the mirror is _________.
questions.explanation:
The image distance (v) is found using the mirror formula: 1/v = 1/f - 1/u. 

With f = -10.0 cm and u = -25.0 cm, 1/v = 1/(-10) - 1/(-25) = -1/10 + 1/25 = (-5 + 2)/50 = -3/50, so v = -50/3 cm.

 The magnification (M) is then M = -v/u = -(-50/3) / (-25) = -2/3 = -0.67. 

The magnitude is 0.67, which corresponds to option C.

questions.questionText: An ammeter measures:
questions.explanation: Ammeters measure the flow of current.

questions.questionText: To convert a density from g/cm³ to kg/m³, you must multiply by:
questions.explanation:
1 g = 10⁻³ kg and 1 cm = 10⁻² m, so 1 cm³ = (10⁻² m)³ = 10⁻⁶ m³.

 Therefore, 1 g/cm³ = (10⁻³ kg) / (10⁻⁶ m³) = 10³ kg/m³ = 1000 kg/m³.

questions.questionText: When two vectors act in the same direction, the resultant is:
questions.explanation: Vectors in same direction add directly.

questions.questionText: The area under a velocity-time graph represents:
questions.explanation: Area under v–t graph equals displacement.

questions.questionText: Which law uses a parallelogram to determine the resultant?
questions.explanation: Parallelogram law finds resultant of two vectors.

questions.questionText: If a vector has magnitude 17 and y-component 15, what is the x-component?
The y-component of a vector lies along:
questions.explanation: The y-component lies along the vertical axis.

questions.questionText: Resistance is defined as:
questions.explanation: Resistance opposes the flow of electric current.

questions.questionText: Two cars move toward each other with speeds 20 m/s and 15 m/s. Their relative speed is:
questions.explanation: Relative speed when approaching = sum = 20 + 15.

questions.questionText: Acceleration is defined as:
options: change in velocity per unit time
questions.explanation: Acceleration = change in velocity / time.

questions.questionText: Vectors that have the same magnitude but opposite direction are called:
questions.explanation: Negative vectors have equal magnitude but opposite direction.

questions.questionText: If a vector is multiplied by −1, the result is:
questions.explanation: Magnitude same but direction reversed.

questions.questionText: Which of the following graphs represents constant velocity motion?
questions.explanation: Horizontal v–t graph means velocity is constant.

questions.questionText: The x-component of a vector lies along:
questions.explanation: The x-component lies along the horizontal axis.

questions.questionText: If red light and green light are mixed together, the resulting color of light is:
questions.explanation: In color addition (mixing light), Red plus Green equals Yellow.

questions.questionText: Relative velocity between two bodies moving in opposite directions equals:
questions.explanation: When moving opposite, speeds add.

questions.questionText: A vector is usually represented graphically by:
questions.explanation: Vectors are represented by arrows showing magnitude and direction.

questions.questionText: A hanging sign with weight W is supported by two cables as shown in a diagram. If the system is in equilibrium, what is the relationship between the vertical components of the cable tensions (Ty1, Ty2) and the weight W?
questions.explanation: Step-by-step conceptual review for this question.

questions.questionText: The SI unit for density is:
questions.explanation:
In the International System of Units (SI), mass is measured in kilograms (kg) and volume is measured in cubic meters (m³).

 Therefore, the SI unit for density is kg/m³.

questions.questionText: If a vector makes 0° with x-axis, its y-component is:
questions.explanation: When angle is 0°, the vector lies entirely along x-axis.

questions.questionText: Density of a substance is defined as:
questions.explanation: Density = mass / volume.

questions.questionText: When you hang a weight on a vertical wire, it experiences:
questions.explanation:
The weight pulls on the wire, causing it to elongate.

 The resulting fractional increase in length is called tensile strain.

questions.questionText: A solenoid with 5000 turns and length 1m carries 15A of current. If no iron core is inserted in the solenoid, what is the magnetic field strength at the center of the solenoid?
questions.explanation:
The magnetic field inside a long solenoid is given by: B = μ₀ * (N / L) * I

Where:- μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ T·m/A (permeability of free space)

- N = number of turns = 5000

- L = length of solenoid = 1 m

- I = current = 15 A

B = (4π × 10⁻⁷) * (5000 / 1) * 15 = 4π × 10⁻⁷ * 75,000 = 3π × 10⁻² T

Thus, the magnetic field at the center of the solenoid is 3π × 10⁻² T.

questions.questionText: The slope of a displacement-time graph gives:
questions.explanation: Slope = velocity.

questions.questionText: If the magnification (m) for an image is positive, the image is:
questions.explanation:
A positive magnification means the image height (h prime) and object height (h) have the same sign, indicating an upright (erect) image.

 Upright images are always virtual in lenses and mirrors.

questions.questionText: Which of the following physical quantities is always constant for an object in free fall near the Earth's surface (neglecting air resistance)?
questions.explanation: In free fall, the only force acting is gravity, resulting in a constant downward acceleration (g ≈ 9.8 m/s²).

questions.questionText: The slope of a velocity-time graph represents:
questions.explanation: Slope = change in velocity / time = acceleration.

questions.questionText: Which color of light has the shortest wavelength?
questions.explanation: Violet light (around 400 nm) has the shortest wavelength in the visible spectrum.

questions.questionText: In a convex mirror, if a ray of light is incident parallel to the principal axis, the reflected ray appears to come from the:
questions.explanation: A convex (diverging) mirror reflects parallel rays such that they appear to diverge from the focal point (F) behind the mirror.

questions.questionText: An EM wave travels from air (n=1.0) into glass (n=1.5). Which property of the wave remains unchanged?
questions.explanation: When a wave passes from one medium to another, its frequency (determined by the source) remains constant, while its speed and wavelength change.

questions.questionText: A car moves at speed of 80.0 km/hr for 1.0 hour to East then back to West in which it travels at speed of 60.0 km/hr for 2.0 hrs. What is the average velocity of the car during its motion?
questions.explanation:
Average velocity is total displacement divided by total time, not total distance divided by total time.

The eastward displacement is 80 km, while the westward displacement is 60 × 2 = 120 km.

Taking east as positive, total displacement = 80 - 120 = -40 km, meaning 40 km west.

Total time = 1 + 2 = 3 hours.

Average velocity = -40/3 ≈ -13.3 km/hr.

questions.questionText: If a charged particle moves parallel to the magnetic field lines, the magnetic force acting on it is:
questions.explanation:
If the velocity v is parallel to the field B, the angle theta is 0 degrees.

 Since F = q v B sin(0 degrees) and sin(0 degrees) = 0, the force is zero.

questions.questionText: 5. Which one of the following statements is correct about the electric field due to a charged spherical solid conductor?
options: It is non-zero constant inside the sphere.
It is parallel to the surface of the sphere.
It is zero inside the sphere.
It is non-zero constant outside the sphere.
questions.explanation: For a charged solid conductor in electrostatic equilibrium, all excess charge resides on the outer surface. According to Gauss's Law, the **electric field inside the sphere is zero** ($E=0$) because there is no net charge enclosed by any Gaussian surface inside the conductor.

questions.questionText: The angle between the Earth's geographic axis and its magnetic axis is known as the angle of:
questions.explanation: The angle of declination is the angle between the true geographic north and the magnetic north at a given point.

questions.questionText: Electromagnetic induction is the process of generating a current in a circuit by:
options: Connecting a permanent magnet to the circuit.
Changing the magnetic flux through the circuit.
Increasing the resistance of the circuit.
questions.explanation: Electromagnetic induction is the phenomenon of inducing an electromotive force (EMF) and, consequently, an electric current by changing the magnetic flux through a conducting loop or coil.

questions.questionText: For an ideal transformer, the power input to the primary coil is **equal** to the power output from the secondary coil. This is an application of the law of:
questions.explanation: Ideal transformers are assumed to be 100 percent efficient, meaning they conserve energy: P input = P output.

questions.questionText: During a charging process by induction, a positively charged rod is brought closed to a neutral metal sphere mounted on an insulated stand without touching it. Then, the metal sphere
options: gains some protons whenever it is grounded.
gains some electrons, whenever it is grounded.
loses some electrons, whenever it is grounded.
becomes positively charged, whenever it is grounded.
questions.explanation:
A positively charged rod attracts free electrons toward the nearby side of the neutral metal sphere.

When the sphere is grounded, electrons can flow from the Earth into the sphere because they are attracted by the positive rod.

Thus, the sphere gains electrons and becomes negatively charged after the grounding and separation process.

questions.questionText: An object has a density of 7860 kg/m³. Given that the density of water is 1000 kg/m³, what is its specific gravity?
questions.explanation:
Specific Gravity (SG) = Density of substance / Density of water. 
So, SG = 7860 kg/m³ / 1000 kg/m³ = 7.86.
 Specific gravity has no units.

questions.questionText: The circular face of a solenoid is placed in front of the north pole of a bar magnet. Which of the following actions does NOT induce an electromotive force (emf) in the solenoid?
options: Moving both the solenoid and the magnet with the same speed in opposite directions
Moving the solenoid towards the magnet
Moving both the solenoid and the magnet with the same speed in the same direction
Keeping the solenoid stationary while bringing the magnet closer to it
questions.explanation:
To induce an electromotive force (emf) via Faraday's law, there must be a change in magnetic flux through the solenoid, which requires relative motion between the solenoid and the magnet. 

Moving both the solenoid and the magnet with the same speed in the same direction means the distance and magnetic flux remain constant, so no emf is induced.

questions.questionText: The primary cause of the Earth's magnetic field is believed to be:
options: Permanent magnetization of the Earth's crust.
Convection currents of molten iron in the outer core.
Large accumulation of static electric charge.
questions.explanation: The most accepted theory attributes the Earth's magnetic field to the 'dynamo effect,' caused by the movement (convection) of molten, electrically conductive iron in the outer core.

questions.questionText: A solenoid is a long coil of wire that generates a magnetic field similar to a:
questions.explanation: The magnetic field produced by a long solenoid is very similar in shape and behavior to that of a simple bar magnet.

questions.questionText: If velocity decreases with time, acceleration is:
questions.explanation: Velocity reduction indicates negative acceleration.

questions.questionText: Light ray is allowed to enter from air medium (n_air =1 ) into water medium of refractive index (n_w= 4/3) at an angle of 30° with the normal to air-water interface (boundary). Which one of the following is correct about the ray of light?
options: The sine of the angle of refraction of the light ray in water is equal to 0.5.
The sine of the angle of refraction of the light ray in water is equal to 0.38
The speed of the light ray in water is 1.33 times that of its speed in air.
The speed of the light ray in water is 0.9 times that of its speed in air.
questions.explanation:
Using Snell's law: n1 * sin(θ1) = n2 * sin(θ2)

Here, n1 = 1 (air), θ1 = 30°, n2 = 4/3 (water). Let θ2 be the angle of refraction in water.

sin(θ2) = n1/n2 * sin(θ1) = (1) / (4/3) * sin(30°) = (3/4) * 0.5 = 0.375 ≈ 0.38

Therefore, the sine of the angle of refraction in water is approximately 0.38.

The speed of light in water is slower than in air by a factor of n_w, so it is not greater than the speed in air.

questions.questionText: If the current in a wire is directed straight up, the magnetic field lines when viewed from above will be directed:
questions.explanation: Using the Right-Hand Grip Rule: thumb up (current direction), curled fingers point in a counter-clockwise direction around the wire.

questions.questionText: When generating electricity in a power plant, the energy source (hydro, wind, coal) provides the:
options: Mechanical energy to turn the turbine.
questions.explanation: All power plants convert a primary source of energy into mechanical energy (motion) to spin the turbine, which then drives the generator to produce electricity.

questions.questionText: The use of a step-up transformer at power stations and step-down transformers near cities is crucial for power transmission primarily because it:
options: Reduces the resistance of the cables.
Minimizes energy loss as heat (I squared R).
questions.explanation: Power is transmitted at very high voltage (V) to reduce the current (I = P/V), thus minimizing energy loss through heat dissipation in the transmission lines, given by Power loss = I squared R.

questions.questionText: To form an image of a distant object, the refracting telescope uses
options: an objective convex lens to collect light and form an image which is magnified by the convex lens of the eyepiece.
convex mirror to collect light and forms an image which is magnified by the convex lens of the eyepiece.
an objective concave lens to collect light and forms an image which is magnified by the concave lens of the eyepiece.
convex mirror to collect light and forms an image which is magnified by the concave lens of the eyepiece.
questions.explanation:
A refracting telescope uses lenses rather than mirrors.

The objective is a convex lens with a long focal length and collects light from the distant object to form a real image.

The eyepiece is also a convex lens and acts as a magnifying glass to enlarge the image formed by the objective.

questions.questionText: 4. Which of the following statements is correct about the components of the velocity of a ball projected up at an angle of $\theta$ with the horizontal? Neglecting the air resistance,
options: the horizontal component of the velocity remains constant throughout the journey.
the horizontal velocity of the ball is equal to zero at the maximum height.
the vertical component of the velocity remains constant throughout its journey.
the vertical component of velocity increases while the horizontal component of velocity decreases.
questions.explanation: In **projectile motion** (neglecting air resistance), there is no horizontal force acting on the object. Therefore, the **horizontal component of the velocity ($v_x$) remains constant** throughout the flight.

questions.questionText: A body starting from rest covers a distance d in time t with uniform acceleration. In what time will it cover a distance of 4d?
questions.explanation:
Since d is proportional to t² (d = 0.5at²), to increase the distance by a factor of 4, the time must increase by a factor of square root of 4, which is 2.
 The new time is 2t.

questions.questionText: Which phenomenon is responsible for a permanent magnet losing its magnetism when heated strongly?
questions.explanation: Strong heating causes increased random thermal energy, which breaks the alignment of the magnetic domains, causing the material to lose its overall magnetic properties.

questions.questionText: A beam of electrons enters a uniform magnetic field, moving perpendicular to the field lines. The electrons will follow a:
questions.explanation: Since the magnetic force F is always perpendicular to the velocity v, it acts as a centripetal force, causing the charged particle to move in a circular path.

questions.questionText: Two people carry a heavy uniform log of length L. If one person is at the extreme left end, where should the other person be to carry exactly half the weight?
options: At L/4 from the right end
At L/3 from the right end
questions.explanation:
For the load to be shared equally, the setup must be symmetrical.
 The log's weight acts at its center (L/2). 
If the two people are at equal distances from the center, they will share the load equally.
 Placing them at the two ends satisfies this condition.

questions.questionText: The force on a charge q moving with velocity v perpendicular to a magnetic field B is given by:
questions.explanation:
The magnitude of the Lorentz force (magnetic force) is F = q v B sin(theta).

 When the velocity is perpendicular to the field (sin(90 degrees) = 1), the formula simplifies to F = q v B.

questions.questionText: If voltage increases while resistance remains constant, current will:
questions.explanation: From Ohm’s law I = V/R.

questions.questionText: Vectors that lie in the same plane are called:
questions.explanation: Coplanar vectors exist in the same plane.

questions.questionText: A ball is thrown upward with a speed of 20 m/s. What is the maximum height it reaches? (Use g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation:
Using v² = v₀² + 2ad. 
At max height, v = 0, a = -g:
 0² = (20 m/s)² + 2 * (-10 m/s²) * H.
 0 = 400 - 20H. 
H = 400 / 20 = 20 m.

questions.questionText: The resultant vector is:
options: Sum of two or more vectors
questions.explanation: The resultant vector is the sum of two or more vectors.

questions.questionText: Which of the following quantities is a vector?
questions.explanation: Displacement has magnitude and direction.

questions.questionText: Why does oil float on water?
options: Oil is less dense than water.
Water is less dense than oil.
questions.explanation:
Objects float in a fluid if their density is less than the fluid's density.
 Since oil floats on water, it must be less dense than water.
 Immiscibility explains why they don't mix, but density explains why one floats on top of the other.

questions.questionText: The SI unit of magnetic field strength (magnetic flux density) is the:
questions.explanation: The SI unit of magnetic field strength (B) is the Tesla (T).

questions.questionText: The operation of an electric motor is based on which principle?
options: Motor effect (force on a current-carrying conductor).
questions.explanation: An electric motor uses the motor effect, which is the force exerted on a current-carrying wire when it is placed in a magnetic field, to produce torque and rotation.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following units is NOT a possible unit of electric field strength?
questions.explanation:
Electric field strength (E) is defined as force per unit charge: E = F/q. 

Its SI unit is Newton per Coulomb (N/C).

 It can also be expressed as potential difference per unit distance: E = V/d, so Volt per meter (V/m) and Joule/(Coulomb * meter) are valid. 

Joule/Coulomb alone is just Volt, which is not a unit of electric field strength.

questions.questionText: A particle has velocity 20 m/s and changes to 30 m/s in 5 s. What is its acceleration?
questions.explanation: Acceleration = (30 − 20)/5 = 2 m/s².

questions.questionText: A body starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at 3.0 m/s². What distance does it cover in the first 4.0 seconds?
The parallelogram law is used for:
questions.explanation: Parallelogram law is a graphical method for vector addition.

questions.questionText: The direction of a vector is determined by:
questions.explanation: Direction is specified by angle relative to axis.

questions.questionText: The process of using a small current to switch on a much larger current is the function of a:
questions.explanation: An electromagnetic relay is a switch that uses a small current in an electromagnet to open or close a circuit that carries a much larger current.

questions.questionText: In an electric circuit, the source of electrical energy is usually:
questions.explanation: A battery supplies electrical energy.

questions.questionText: In a generator, the direction of the induced current in the coil is found using:
questions.explanation: Fleming's Right-Hand Rule (generator rule) is specifically used to determine the direction of the induced current (or EMF) when a conductor moves in a magnetic field.

questions.questionText: The use of split-ring commutators in a rotating coil leads to the production of:
questions.explanation: A split-ring commutator acts as a mechanical rectifier, reversing the external connections every half-turn to ensure the output current flows in only one direction, resulting in Direct Current (DC).

questions.questionText: Ohm’s law states that:
questions.explanation: Ohm’s law: V = IR.

questions.questionText: Which of the following represents a vector?
questions.explanation: 20 N east has magnitude and direction, so it is a vector.

questions.questionText: Which of the following colors of visible light has the lowest energy?
questions.explanation:
Energy is proportional to frequency (E is proportional to f). 

Red light has the lowest frequency (and longest wavelength) in the visible spectrum, meaning it has the lowest photon energy.

questions.questionText: In parallelogram law, the resultant vector is represented by:
questions.explanation: The diagonal of the parallelogram gives the resultant vector.

questions.questionText: If the angle of incidence of a light ray striking a boundary between two media is 0 degrees, the angle of refraction will be:
questions.explanation: If the angle of incidence is 0 degrees (the ray is traveling along the normal), the ray passes straight through, and the angle of refraction is also 0 degrees.

questions.questionText: If acceleration is zero, which quantity remains constant?
questions.explanation: Zero acceleration means velocity does not change.

questions.questionText: According to Coulomb’s law, electrostatic force is inversely proportional to:
questions.explanation: F ∝ 1/r².

questions.questionText: Which method uses a parallelogram to find the resultant of two vectors?
questions.explanation: Parallelogram law determines resultant of two vectors graphically.

questions.questionText: A light ray is traveling from medium 1 (n1 = 1.3) to medium 2 (n2 = 1.5). The light ray will bend:
questions.explanation: When light travels from an optically less dense medium (lower n) to an optically denser medium (higher n), it bends towards the normal.

questions.questionText: The slope of displacement-time graph gives:
questions.explanation: Slope represents velocity.

questions.questionText: A material breaks with very little plastic deformation. This material is said to be:
questions.explanation: Brittle materials, like glass or ceramics, fracture suddenly without significant plastic deformation (stretching or bending) once the stress exceeds their elastic limit.

questions.questionText: Two point charges of +3 μC and -6 μC are 2 m apart. What is the magnitude of the electrostatic force between them? (k = 9 × 10⁹ Nm²/C²)
A body starts with velocity 5 m/s and accelerates at 3 m/s² for 4 s. Final velocity is:
An aluminum wire (Y = 7.0 x 10¹⁰ Pa) and a steel wire (Y = 20 x 10¹⁰ Pa) of the same dimensions are subjected to the same tensile stress. Which statement is correct?
options: The strain in the aluminum wire is greater.
The strain in the steel wire is greater.
questions.explanation:
Strain = Stress / Y.
 Since both wires have the same stress, the wire with the lower Young's Modulus (Y) will have the greater strain.
 Aluminum has a lower Y than steel, so it will experience more strain (stretch more).

questions.questionText: Electric discharge occurs when:
questions.explanation: Discharge is the sudden flow of charge.

questions.questionText: If A = 6i and B = 8j, what is the magnitude of A + B?
questions.explanation: Resultant magnitude √(6² + 8²) = 10.

questions.questionText: If displacement-time graph is curved upward, acceleration is:
questions.explanation: Curving upward indicates increasing velocity.

questions.questionText: The maximum velocity attained by an EM wave is in:
questions.explanation: The speed of light (c) is the maximum speed an EM wave can travel, and this occurs in a vacuum.

questions.questionText: An electron moving North enters a magnetic field directed East. The magnetic force on the electron is directed:
questions.explanation:
Using the Right-Hand Palm Rule for a positive charge (or the three-finger rule), the force would be Upward.

 Since the electron is negatively charged, the force is in the opposite direction, which is Downward.

questions.questionText: The property of plasticity is essential in which of the following processes?
options: Manufacturing new goods by molding and pressure treatments.
Building bridges that flex and return to shape.
questions.explanation:
Plasticity is the ability of a material to undergo permanent deformation. 
This property is crucial for processes like forging, molding, and stamping, where a material needs to be shaped into a new, permanent form.

questions.questionText: A light ray that passes through the center of curvature of a spherical mirror after reflection:
options: Travels parallel to the principal axis.
questions.explanation: A ray passing through the center of curvature (C) hits the mirror surface perpendicularly (along the normal) and thus is reflected back along the same path (retrace).

questions.questionText: The ratio of tensile stress to tensile strain is known as:
questions.explanation:
Young's Modulus (Y) is a measure of a material's stiffness.

 It is defined as the ratio of tensile stress to tensile strain: 
Y = Stress / Strain.
